Expectations
Our Values
Our Values
We set extremely high expectations at Holmleigh Park - because we know that if we accept second best from students, we aren't giving them the best education possible.
This means asking students to live up to our three values:
Our rules aren't particularly complicated, but we do insist that absolutely everyone gets the basics right: Arriving correctly dressed and fully equipped, working hard and not disrupting anyone's learning, being kind and courteous in the playground, and completing all homework on time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome - Holmleigh Park High School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Headteacher’s Welcome
Headteacher’s Welcome
It's my pleasure to welcome you to our website.
Holmleigh Park is an ambitious academy located in Tuffley, Gloucester. We believe that all children have limitless potential, and are proud to offer a comprehensive education to all students in our local community.
We expect all staff, students and parents to embrace our three principles - Work Hard, Be Kind, Take Responsibility - so that our students leave school as ambitious, confident and successful young adults with the highest standards of integrity.
Everything we do is underpinned by three key drivers:
Outcomes – Our core purpose is ensuring students leave with the best possible exam results, so they can access the most ambitious and aspirational destinations and step into adulthood with confidence and choice.
Opportunities – We want every student to take part in enriching experiences that build confidence, create lasting memories and allow them to represent the school with pride. We believe in students leaving a legacy and shaping the culture of the school for those who follow.
Disruption-Free Learning – We set the highest expectations for student conduct. Every student is expected to show the very best version of themselves so that every lesson is calm, focused and allows all learners to thrive.
We are proud members of the Greenshaw Learning Trust, a ‘family’ of like-minded schools, which collaborate to provide mutual support, share their good practice and learn from each other, whilst retaining and developing their own distinctive character.
I hope that this website gives you a flavour of our school, but if you're able to, please do come and visit us to see it for yourself. We'd be delighted to show you round - please email contact@hphigh.co.uk to arrange a visit.
Dan Hudson Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Sixth Form
Sixth Form
Information
Super Curriculum
Super Curriculum
At HP High Sixth Form, we are keen for our students to engage with their subjects, beyond what their classroom teachers cover. Our super curriculum is designed to give sixth form pupils the chance to explore different aspects of their subjects - in a range of formats. These activities include, but are not limited to, watching videos, reading articles, and attending online lectures.
The intent behind the super curriculum is to help our students to develop a passion for their subjects. It also serves the dual purpose of strengthening future applications, whether it is for university, apprenticeships, or work. These lists are not exhaustive, and we encourage pupils to speak to teachers if they want any more suggestions.

Information
Careers
Please use the menu to the right to get started.

Information
Information
Our Character Programme
Enrichment
Enrichment
In September 2025, we introduced HP Enrichment, an exciting new initiative that embeds extra-curricular clubs directly into the school timetable. This ensures every student has the opportunity to explore new interests, develop skills, and take part in enriching activities as part of their school day. A copy of the activities on offer can be found in the Enrichment booklet below.
Our sports teams continue to train and compete in fixtures after school. Please see below for details of the days and activities.
What is HP Enrichment?
At Holmleigh Park, we believe that every child has limitless potential and one of the key ways we help them realise it is by offering incredible opportunities beyond the classroom. That’s why Opportunities is one of our three key drivers, alongside Outcomes and Disruption-Free Learning.
We want our students to leave school not only with excellent exam results, but also with the confidence, ambition and integrity to succeed in life. Enrichment plays a vital role in that journey.
From September, every student will take part in a weekly extracurricular club as part of their school timetable. Whether it’s sport, music, debating, creative arts or STEM, our programme offers something for everyone. These experiences build character, spark passions and create lasting memories alongside helping students to be proud of themselves, their school and their community. This is enrichment for all, and it sits at the heart of Holmleigh Park life.

Information
Information
Our Character Programme
extra-curricular
extra-curricular
Alongside our Enrichment Programme, we also offer the below extracurricular activities to support students in developing skills and interests beyond the classroom.
AFTER SCHOOL SPORT AT HP
Our sports teams train after school from 3.00–4.00pm on the days listed below. All pupils are welcome to take part – they just need to bring their HP PE kit and join in.
Tuesday Y9 & Y10 boys rugby Y9 & Y10 girls football
Wednesday Y7 & Y8 boys rugby Y7 & Y8 girls football
AFTER SCHOOL CLUBS
Y9 & Y10 Drama Club is run by Mr Conway on Thursdays after school in the Theatre from 3pm-4pm.
The GCSE Coursework Catch-Up Art Club is a supportive after-school session designed to help students stay on track with their art and design projects. It provides time, space, and guidance to complete or refine coursework, experiment with materials, and develop ideas for their portfolios. Whether you’re finishing sketchbook pages, improving final pieces, or exploring new techniques, this club is the perfect opportunity to focus and make creative progress towards their GCSE in art. It is held in H16 on Wednesdays after school 3pm-4pm with Miss Martin.
Art Club - Would you like to see a piece of your artwork displayed in the Royal Academy of Art London? We are looking for students to create a piece of work to be entered into the Royal Academy Young Artist competition. This is open to all students and will run on a Thursday after school 3pm-4pm in H17 with Miss Parker.
Axiom Maths Club - Every obstacle is just a puzzle to be solved! Join us for a fun session exploring maths, enjoy getting stuck as well as getting unstuck. Mr Tarr runs the Y7 club on Thursdays in M9 and Mrs Mihoc runs the Y8 club on Fridays, both running 3pm-4pm. Contact s.tarr@hphigh.co.uk or r.mihoc@hphigh.co.uk for more information.
Year 10 Spanish Workshop - All students studying Spanish for GCSE are welcome to come along to practise exam skills, revise topics, get homework help or build their confidence with speaking in smaller groups or with additional support. Each session will focus on a different skill and can be student-led, so if you have a skill or topic you want to focus on, it can be tailored to the group attending. This runs every Wednesday from 3pm-4pm with Miss Grinham in A6.
HP Voices - If you love to sing join HP Voices - our school choir. This is your opportunity to have fun singing with others, learn new skills, relieve stress, experience performing in a range of venues and make new friends from different year groups. We will be singing everything from pop hits and musical theatre to classical epics. Students from all year groups are welcome to join. No experience is needed and no audition is required. For more information, see Mrs Greenow in the Music Department. The choir will start on Wednesday 4th November and will run every Wednesday from 3-4pm in MU1.
Homework club is held every day in IT3 after school. It is held in a computer room and offers support for anyone requiring any extra help completing their homework. It runs 3pm-4pm from Monday to Thursday and 3pm-3:30pm on Fridays.
Champions Hour is held for Y11 students after school in the library from 4pm-5pm. It offers a space for students to complete supervised independent work to increase their chances of success. It has a lovely atmosphere for studying (and always a tin of biscuits!).
LUNCHTIME CLUBS
Christian Union is held on Thursday lunchtimes in M8.
Maths Higher GCSE is held on Tuesdays in M8. Open to all students to gain confidence in Maths exam questions.
Young Carers - We think our Young Carers are amazing and deserve to be celebrated! Each Wednesday lunchtime we get together in Safeguarding to have a treat, relax and have fun with other young carers. It is a great opportunity to know that you are not alone and can feel supported by other students and the Safeguarding team. Newcomers are always welcome!!
BEFORE SCHOOL CLUBS
Breakfast club is held in the Theatre every morning before line up between 8am - 8:25am. It is run by our Teaching Assistants, who provide a warm welcome to start the day. Pupils can help themselves to free breakfast items to set themselves up for the day ahead.

Information
Careers Advice and Destinations
Careers Advice and Destinations
Our Sixth Form Team are very experienced in providing expert advice and guidance for students.
Each year, the vast majority of our students go on to university. Our UCAS coordinator will guide you through the process, from choosing a course and carefully selecting which universities to apply for to crafting a compelling personal statement, you will receive a huge amount of support at every stage. As a result, our students go to top universities across the country each year. We offer additional, personalised support for students considering applying for medicine or Oxbridge.
Apprenticeships are becoming more popular each year, with some of the most prestigious programmes now receiving considerably more applicants per place than Oxford and Cambridge! Our sixth form team will help you navigate this complicated landscape, and apply for the right programme for you. You will receive exactly the same level of personalised advice as all University applicants.
We are proud to partner with unifrog, which gives all students access to powerful tools to help you refine your interests, find the right course, and pitch your applications at exactly the right destinations.

HP Home-School Communication Protocol
We encourage all parents and carers to review our Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) webpage before contacting the school, as it may address your question promptly.
Contacting Holmleigh Park
Preferred Method of Contact: Email
Email ensures a digital record of communication and allows staff the flexibility to respond effectively. If required, a follow-up telephone call or meeting can be arranged after the initial email contact.
Years 7-11: Text 07860054561, including the student’s name, tutor group, and reason for absence.
Years 12-13: Call the Sixth Form direct line at 01452 393760 or email sixthform@hphigh.co.uk
Communication Tiers
Holmleigh Park staff aim to reply to emails during school hours (8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday to Friday), excluding weekends, Bank Holidays, and school holidays.
Tier 1: Specific Concerns
Target Response Time: Within 1 to 2 school days, depending on the query
Attendance Concerns: Email Attendance@hphigh.co.uk
Safeguarding Concerns: Email Safeguarding@hphigh.co.uk or call the school
Behaviour Issues: Email the relevant Head of Year or the Head of Behaviour. Contact details are available on the school’s Contact Details page: https://www.hphigh.co.uk/contact-us
Academic Concerns: Email the relevant Director of Faculty (see the Contact Details page for their information).
Special Educational Needs: Email SENCO@hphigh.co.uk
General Queries: contact@hphigh.co.uk. The contact@ team will handle general queries. If unable to answer, they will forward your email to the appropriate staff member.
Tier 2: Senior Leadership Team
Target Response Time: Within 1 to 5 school days, depending on the query
Each year group is overseen by a Senior Leadership Team (SLT) member, who supports pastoral care and helps resolve serious or previously unresolved issues or enquiries. Contact information is available on the Contact Details page:https://www.hphigh.co.uk/contact-us
Target Response Time: Within 1 to 10 school days, depending on the query
For complaints at Stage 2, please review the Complaints Policy to ensure all prior steps (Tiers 1-3) have been taken. The Headteacher may delegate responses to appropriate staff where necessary.Complaints Policy: http://www.hphigh.co.uk
For phone queries, please contact our main reception by calling 01452 301381:
General Enquiries: Reception staff will assist where possible or guide you to the appropriate staff member’s email.
Specific Staff Requests: Messages will be taken and emailed to the relevant staff member, who will respond once their teaching commitments allow. For faster communication, we recommend emailing the staff member directly.
Communication Guidelines
Respectful CommunicationWe expect all communication to remain polite and respectful. Our pupils and staff are entitled to a safe and respectful environment. Concerns should be addressed courteously, and we will take appropriate action if these standards are not met.
Pre-Booked Meetings OnlyAll meetings with staff must be scheduled in advance. Drop-in meetings cannot be accommodated due to teaching and duty commitments.
Formal ComplaintsFor formal complaints, refer to the Complaints Policy for timescales and procedures, which may differ from the response times outlined above.http://www.hphigh.co.uk
We appreciate your cooperation in adhering to these protocols to ensure effective communication between home and school.

pageCache.text:
Information
Information
Our Character Programme
School Colours
School Colours
Students who make significant contributions to the school can be awarded with Junior, Half or Full Colours. Students must be nominated for their contribution to one of four areas:
Academic - for exceptional achievement in lessons
Culture - for exceptional contributions to art, music, drama or other cultural areas
Sport - for exceptional contributions to the school's sports teams
Values - for being an exceptional role model and embodying the school's values
Students can be nominated by staff, and all applications are reviewed by the Colours Committee.
Junior Colours
Junior Colours are awarded to students who have made a significant contribution the school. Students are eligible for consideration from Year 7 onwards.
Junior Colours confer a striped blue and white badge, shown below.
Half Colours
Half Colours are awarded to students who have made a significant and extended contribution the school. Students are eligible for consideration from Year 9 onwards.
Half Colours confer a fully blue badge, shown below.
Full Colours
Full Colours are awarded only to those students who have made exceptional contributions to academic, culture, sport or the school community over their time at Holmleigh Park. They are very difficult to achieve, and students become eligible for consideration in Year 11 and the Sixth Form.
Students who receive Full Colours are permitted to wear a special tie, shown to the right.
The light blue colour reflects the "Blues" which are awarded by some of the UK's top universities for exceptional sporting achievements.

pageCache.text:
Information
Information
Our Character Programme
Student Leadership
Student Leadership
Nurturing student leadership is a significant component of our mission and dedication to our students. We hold great ambitions for our students and firmly believe that fostering their leadership skills contributes significantly to positively impacting our community and enhancing their opportunities in life.
At KS3 and KS4, students have the exciting opportunity to join our Student Council team, while in KS5, they can aspire to become exceptional House Captains.
At Holmleigh Park, we recognise the value of student voice. It is our utmost priority to ensure that every pupil relishes their school experience and feels that their voice holds significant worth. To achieve this, we have established a dedicated Student Council that will actively contribute to this endeavour.
The members of our Student Council have been elected by their fellow students, serving as the dedicated representatives of the student voice. With one representative for each house, totalling four members per year group, the council meets regularly to exchange ideas, devise strategies, and provide feedback, all aimed at enhancing the overall school experience for every student. Furthermore, they maintain a consistent line of communication with the Senior Leadership Team (SLT), ensuring that feedback is shared and proposals are presented, fostering strong collaboration between staff and students.
KS3 & KS4 Student council
At our Sixth Form, students have the exciting opportunity to apply for the positions of House Captain and Vice House Captain. Working closely with the Head of Houses, the House Captains play a pivotal role in leading our house systems, creating opportunities for students to engage in various house competitions and proudly represent their respective houses.
Beyond fostering a vibrant house culture and a strong sense of belonging, House Captains also have their own distinct responsibilities. These encompass the following roles:
Captain of Community
Within these roles, both House Captains and Vice Captains collaborate closely with their respective Head of House, aiming to enhance the overall student experience here at Holmleigh Park. They achieve this by actively encouraging student participation in arts and sports, promoting student involvement and volunteering within the school and local communities, and seeking and listening to the student voice, ensuring that every individual feels appreciated and heard. Throughout the year, they will organise charity initiatives and fundraising events, embodying our commitment to giving back and making a difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Curriculum - Holmleigh Park High School
pageCache.text:
Information
Information
Our Curriculum
Our Curriculum
At Holmleigh Park High School we believe that all students are entitled to a curriculum that provides intellectual, cultural, moral, creative and physical enrichment. We provide a broad, balanced and rigorous curriculum that inspires and challenges students to be the very best they can throughout school and into their future.
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to ensure that students learning develops progressively in each subject. The curriculum is constantly reviewed and is a product of collaboration between teachers in the school and within the trust.
The curriculum has been designed with the needs of all learners taken into consideration, especially those with additional learning needs. Further information can be found in our SEN report, available on our policy and document page.
Each subject has developed a curriculum that is built around core concepts and knowledge and the understanding of these is fundamental to becoming successful learners.
The curriculum at Key Stage 3 (Years 7, 8 and 9) focusses on giving students the broadest experience as possible in the arts, languages, humanities and technical subjects, while maintaining a strong focus on the core subjects of English, mathematics, science, PSHE, RS and PE. In addition to this choir is a valued part of our curriculum in Year 7 and 8.
At Key Stage 4 (Years 10 and 11), the curriculum is a combination of both core and optional subjects that is structured to allow for maximum flexibility of choice. There is a broad range of both academic and vocational subjects which allow students to study the arts, humanities, languages, sport, business and much more.
In our Sixth Form (Years 12 and 13) we offer an academic or technical curriculum covering a broad range of subjects that will enable students to progress on to top universities or into competitive apprenticeships.
To find out more about our curriculum, please contact our Deputy Headteacher (Academic), Mr Andy Park (a.park@hphigh.co.uk).
English
Why is it important to study English?
English is the foundation for all effective communication. The study of English encourages an imaginative and thought-provoking engagement of language as well as inspiring curiosity in the world around us.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in English?
Exploring the power of language through a broad and diverse range of texts enables you to become a confident writer, articulate speaker and thoughtful reader. English provides a window into other worlds, times and cultures as well as holding a mirror to ourselves to examine our identities and roles in society.
What skills and knowledge will you have when you leave HPHS?
You will be confident users of core knowledge that stretches across KS3, 4 and KS5 and be able to apply that knowledge to both fiction and non-fiction texts. You will have become assured critical readers, adept creative writers and skilful orators. Clarity of communication is what will drive success in later life and so, within the curriculum, we endeavour to mould self-assured individuals that can express their opinions and develop their own voices.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying English will open both at school and beyond?
English is fundamental for future success in all elements of life, whether you choose to pursue higher education or employment. From writing a job application to writing an award-winning novel, English will provide you with an array of pathways and opportunities.
Success in English can lead you to an exciting list of possible opportunities including law, journalism, teaching, media, public relations, human resources, local government, social work, marketing, travel and tourism and publishing.
Mathematics
Why is it important to study Mathematics?
Mathematics is the language of the modern world. It empowers us to interpret data, solve problems, and make informed decisions in everyday life and work. From budgeting to navigating technology, maths underpins critical aspects of society, science, and innovation. Studying maths helps develop logical thinking, perseverance, and precision, skills vital for all careers and lifelong learning. It builds confidence in problem-solving and equips students to understand the world around them, from patterns in nature to the algorithms behind digital tools.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in Mathematics ?
Through the study of mathematics you will develop an understanding and enjoyment of the subject by learning a rich and challenging programme of study. You will learn to become fluent in the fundamentals of Mathematics, reason mathematically and use your acquired knowledge to solve routine and non-routine problems.
What skills and knowledge will you have when you leave HPHS?
You should leave school as a confident problem-solver with strong reasoning and analytical skills. You will be able to communicate mathematical ideas clearly, interpret and evaluate data, and apply logical thinking to unfamiliar problems. You will be resilient, precise, and able to select appropriate strategies to tackle a range of tasks. These skills support success in further study, the workplace, and daily life.
You will have a solid understanding of number, algebra, ratio, geometry, statistics, probability and will understand how mathematical concepts connect and apply across topics. You will be numerate and use appropriate methods and tools to solve problems in real-world contexts. You will know how to interpret results, evaluate accuracy, and reflect on their approaches.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying Mathematics will open both at school and beyond?
Maths is a gateway to further study in sciences, economics, computing, and engineering, as well as A-Levels and vocational qualifications. It opens doors to diverse careers - from finance and medicine to design, coding, and construction. Strong maths skills are valued by employers and are essential in many apprenticeship routes and degree pathways. Studying maths builds a foundation for informed citizenship and lifelong opportunity.
Science
Why is it important to study Science?
Science is full of awe and wonder. Studying Science prepares you to understand, interact with and value the complex web of life, processes and the environment we live in.
Science enables you to develop as well-rounded global citizens capable of making informed decisions.
What is the knowledge you will learn in Science ?
Through the study of Biology, Chemistry and Physics you will develop an understanding of the key concepts, leading to the ability to draw, challenge and explore conclusions through practical science.
What are the skills you will gain in Science ?
Science will develop your grasp of the underlying concepts affecting our earth and living things. You will have acquired dexterity and manipulation skills to be able to test a hypothesis. You will have the confidence to display data and logically reason and answer opposing questions to your data.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying Science will open both at school and beyond?
Given its unique breadth, Science allows students to access a wide range of further education and careers both in and out of the STEM subjects. Studying science leads to a vast range of professions and careers, from astronomy to zoology.
Art and Design
Why is it important to study Art and Design?
Art is within everything we do and is an essential visual language. We inspire and challenge you to experiment, create, invent and become an original thinker. Art will help you to develop a passion and curiosity for all that the world of Art can offer.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in Art and Design ?
In Art, you will learn about the visual elements of line, tone, texture, colour, shape, form and pattern. As well as this, you will explore different skills and media, including painting, printing, textiles, photoshop and 3-dimensional design.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying Art and Design will open both at school and beyond?
In Art and Design many of our students have taken the subject further and been involved in careers such as illustration, graphics, surface design, architecture, fashion as well as jobs in art history.
Business and Enterprise
Why is it important to study Business and Enterprise?
Business and Enterprise develops knowledge and understanding of local and national businesses and the issues they face. You will demonstrate enterprise skills and have to think like real business leaders to creatively solve realistic problems to make decisions.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in Business and Enterprise?
You will develop a range of skills that will include allowing you to develop as an effective and independent learner through questioning data, constructing well-argued responses and developing an understanding of business. You will gain knowledge of how businesses operate, the reasons behind them and the issues faced locally and nationally.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying Business and Enterprise will open both at school and beyond?
Students will develop their understanding and skills that are useful for any career path, including; presenting, report writing, primary and secondary research as well as specific business skills such as finance, accounting, sales, marketing, human resources, administration and production.
Apprenticeships are popular with our students as many have gone onto form careers with top 100 UK companies, including leading organisations such as Barnett Waddingham. Other examples include apprenticeships in accounting, finance, human resources, operations, economics, sales and marketing. Students can continue their studies at university, where they can further develop their understanding of Business Studies. Many have gone on to study management, accounting, project management and international business.
Criminology
Why is it important to study Criminology?
In essence, Criminology is the study of crime and criminal behaviour, how and why it may occur, as well as methods to try and prevent it. When studying the subject, you will analyse both individual criminal behaviour and wider societal or sociological trends as well as apply academic criminal theories to real-life examples in order to attempt to discover the reasons why an individual may commit a crime. Criminology is a multifaceted discipline that requires you to draw on numerous other fields, including history, anthropology, psychology, sociology and criminal law. Criminology offers a method of trying to understand the causes of crime and what strategies offer solutions for its reduction and mitigation; and the evaluation of existing structures within the criminal justice system in England and Wales.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in Criminology ?
You will learn how to successfully analyse situations of criminality and the aims of punishment, apply academic theory to real-life case studies, assess the verdicts of criminal cases and consider their validity, evaluate the strengths and limitations of a variety of aspects of the criminal justice system, from agencies within the justice system to the relationships between these agencies and how they approach social control. You will develop the skills needed to articulate yourself about key concepts and ideas relating to the study of crime and criminal behaviour and will develop your skills of examination, research and enquiry.
What are the pathways and opportunities that studying Criminology will open both at school and beyond?
Studying criminology will open several pathways for students to see whether a career in the criminal justice system is desirable or not. For example, once the Applied Diploma is completed, the study of Criminology at university can lead to a career as a civil service administrator, community development worker, crime scene investigator, pathologist, police officer, prison officer, probation worker, social worker, youth worker, barrister, criminal psychologist, counsellor, paralegal, lawyer social researcher, police staff investigator and many more. However, if a career within the criminal justice system is not the desired outcome, the study of criminology will help students to enter their chosen study/career path using the variety of skills they have obtained.
Drama
Why is it important to study Drama?
The Performing Arts are a powerful force in shaping and defining our futures. Music & Drama are part of our everyday life and are familiar to everyone. They have their origins in ancient traditions whilst also reflecting contemporary experience. Through the teaching of Drama at Holmleigh Park, we aim to broaden the horizons of all our students, enabling them to fulfil their potential and make positive changes to the world around them. In lessons, we will study vocal, physical and character skills, learning how to better communicate with those around us. However, in addition to the specific Drama skills that our students will learn, the Performing Arts also teach us vital soft skills such as confidence, problem solving and teamwork, skills vital for whatever our young people wish to do in the future.
What are the skills and knowledge you will learn in Drama?
Studying Drama equips students with a wide range of knowledge, applicable to both drama and other fields. Students will learn to develop characters, explore performance styles, and understand theatrical conventions and practitioners. Specifically, these include elements such as stagecraft, dramatic structure and the social, cultural or historic context of plays. In addition, students will also learn about dramatic conventions, genres and practitioners and how these can be better used to communicate artistic intention with an audience.
